text:
sarah.k: Heads-up: Customer (private VPC) reporting intermittent TLS failures to api.redwood-inference.com from their inference nodes. ~3-7% of requests fail with TLS handshake timeout. Starts after a few minutes of steady traffic.

james.n: Do we have a reproducible trace / error sample? Is DNS timing out or TLS failing after TCP established?

sarah.k: They gave this curl output from one of the pods: `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"` -> shows `* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (3.210.45.12) port 443 (#0)` then `* TLS handshake timeout` (retries succeed).

customer_ops: Adding more detail: happens across multiple nodes in the ASG, only from this private subnet. No issues from their public bastion. They run a managed NAT gateway + custom NACLs and strict SGs.

mike.netops: Sounds like return-path or ephemeral port blocking. With a managed NAT you still need ephemeral port range allowed in NACLs since NACLs are stateless. If they deny ephemeral range inbound, SYN-ACKs won't reach the node.

james.n: Can they share `tcpdump` from the failing pod during a failure? Need to see SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK. Also dig + curl with `--resolve` to confirm DNS isn't flipping A records.

sarah.k: They attached a small tcpdump snippet (filtered):
```
14:23:02.123456 IP pod-1.10.0.5.49192 > api.redwood-inference.com.443: Flags [S], seq 1234567, win 64240
14:23:03.234567 IP api.redwood-inference.com.443 > 10.0.5.10.49192: Flags [S.], seq 7654321, ack 1234568, win 65535
14:23:03.234580 IP 10.0.5.10.49192 > api.redwood-inference.com.443: Flags [R], seq 1234568, win 0
```
Followed by successful attempt a few seconds later where ACK completes and TLS proceeds.

mike.netops: Interesting: node sends R after getting SYN-ACK. That implies either the pod/host is already torn down or kernel is rejecting because it thinks connection wasn't initiated. Could be SNAT port translation mismatch if ephemeral port gets rewritten by an intermediate device and NACL denies the return.

alexa-bot: Noted. Checking customer's NACL rules provided earlier: their inbound NACL has an explicit DENY 100 for port range 49152-65535 and an ALLOW 200 for ephemeral range 32768-49151. Outbound allows 443 but outbound ephemeral ALLOW is missing.

james.n: That's the smoking gun — stateless NACLs require both directions allowed for ephemeral ranges. If inbound denies 49152-65535 but outbound uses ephemeral above 49152 after SNAT, replies will be dropped. Two mitigations: (1) widen allowed ephemeral ranges on inbound to match outbound SNAT result, or (2) set their NAT to keep ports in lower ephemeral range.

sarah.k: Also they mentioned an inline TLS termination/proxy in their environment doing SNI rewrite for egress inspection. Could be rewriting SNI and causing the TLS server to send a different certificate occasionally (retries hit different proxy instance).

mike.netops: Ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` during a failure to capture cert chain. If SNI rewrite is inconsistent, packet path differences + NACLs could make some handshake attempts hit different proxies.

customer_ops: We ran `openssl s_client` — sometimes we see cert for `inspection-proxy.local` when handshake fails, but curl shows timeout not cert mismatch.

james.n: That aligns with a proxy that accepts TCP but stalls TLS. Combined with NACL issues you can get half-open handshakes that the client RSTs. For now, recommended steps:
- Allow ephemeral port range 32768-65535 inbound/outbound in NACLs (both directions).
- Add an ALLOW for established return ports in SGs/iptables if they have host-level firewall.
- Temporarily disable SNI rewrite/inspection on one node to test.

mike.netops: I'll craft a minimal NACL patch snippet they can apply:
```
# inbound NACL: allow ephemeral range
rule 150 allow tcp 32768-65535 0.0.0.0/0
# outbound NACL: ensure 32768-65535 allowed
rule 150 allow tcp 32768-65535 0.0.0.0/0
```
And ensure no explicit DENY entry with a lower rule number overlaps. NACLs evaluate by rule number order.

sarah.k: Customer applied the inbound change and we saw immediate reduction in TLS timeouts during a 10m soak (0/400 failed). They also disabled SNI rewrite on a test node — also looks clean.

james.n: Great. Follow-ups: ask them to review their NAT port allocation (some managed NATs allocate ports >49152) and make NACL ranges symmetric, and if they need stricter control, use stateful SGs + NAT gateway instead of trying to be strict at NACL layer.

customer_ops: Thanks — filing a change request to make NACL symmetric and will schedule a maintenance window to remove the explicit DENY. We'll update once NAT port ranges are confirmed.

sarah.k: I'll convert this to a support ticket with root cause: stateless NACL blocking ephemeral return ports + intermittent SNI inspection path. Recommend doc link: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nacl-rules.html (rule ordering) and add Redwood KB link on ephemeral ports for inference nodes.

alexa-bot: Support ticket created: #SUP-45512. Closing thread for now, will reopen if customer sees recurrence. :white_check_mark:
